slides.title: Ethernet & Wi-Fi Standards
content: Ethernet (IEEE 802.3) is a wired networking technology used in LANs that provides high-speed and reliable communication using MAC addresses
It operates at the data link and physical layers and uses Ethernet frames and CSMA/CD for data transmission
Wi-Fi (IEEE 802.11) is a wireless networking technology that uses radio waves to connect devices without physical cables
Wi-Fi operates on frequencies like 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz and provides mobility and flexibility for modern networks

slides.title: Ethernet Standards Evolution
content: Ethernet standards define speeds and transmission media such as 10BASE-T (10 Mbps), 100BASE-TX (100 Mbps), and 1000BASE-T (1 Gbps)
Modern Ethernet supports high speeds like 10 Gbps, 40 Gbps, and 100 Gbps for data centers and enterprise networks
Wireless standards like 802.11n, 802.11ac, and 802.11ax (Wi-Fi 6) provide increasing speed and efficiency
These standards ensure compatibility and scalability across different networking devices and environments

slides.title: Ethernet Switching
content: Ethernet switching is a technology that connects devices in a LAN and forwards data frames using MAC addresses
Switches maintain MAC address tables to send data only to the intended device, reducing unnecessary traffic
They support unicast, broadcast, and multicast communication for efficient data transfer
Switching improves network performance, security, and scalability compared to hubs

slides.title: VLAN (Virtual LAN)
content: A VLAN is a logical grouping of devices in a network that creates separate broadcast domains within the same physical network
It uses IEEE 802.1Q tagging to identify VLAN-specific traffic in Ethernet frames
VLANs improve security by isolating network traffic and enhance performance by reducing broadcast traffic
Inter-VLAN communication requires routing using a router or Layer 3 switch

slides.title: Data Link Protocols
content: Data link protocols operate at Layer 2 of the OSI model and ensure reliable communication between directly connected devices
PPP (Point-to-Point Protocol) provides encapsulation, authentication, and error detection for direct communication links
HDLC (High-Level Data Link Control) is a bit-oriented protocol that ensures reliable data transfer with framing and flow control
These protocols handle error detection using CRC and manage data transmission over physical links

slides.title: Spanning Tree Protocol (STP)
content: STP (Spanning Tree Protocol) is a network protocol that prevents loops in Ethernet networks by creating a loop-free topology
It elects a root bridge and assigns port roles like root port, designated port, and blocked port
It uses Bridge Protocol Data Units (BPDUs) to exchange topology information and detect network changes
STP ensures network stability, prevents broadcast storms, and provides redundancy for failover
